sentences.text: Revenue compounded from $4,860.4m in FY2016 [F1] to $14,342.9m in FY2025 [F10], a 12.8% CAGR [F198], though the path was a step change rather than steady growth.

Revenue rose 89.1% to $16,071.7m in FY2021 [D241][F6] on REGEN-COV sales to the U.S. government under a September 2021 supply agreement [P39], taking US REGEN-COV product sales to $5,828.0m [S48] from $185.7m in FY2020 [S47].
Those sales did not recur: revenue fell 24.3% to $12,172.9m in FY2022 [D292][F7] and US REGEN-COV sales were $0.0m [S49], as the filing notes the 2021 sales did not continue into 2022 [P33].
Since FY2022 revenue has compounded 5.6% a year [D767], while operating margin fell from its FY2021 high of 55.7% [F26] to 24.9% in FY2025 [F30].

In FY2025 net product sales fell 17.3% [D506], taking 9.3pp off revenue growth [D507], while collaboration revenue, now 51.1% of revenue [D521], rose 21.0% to $7,331.2m [D522][S22] and added 9.0pp [D523].
US EYLEA sales fell 42.4% to $2,747.8m [D577][S43], a 14.2pp drag [D578], on lower volumes from competitive pressure, a lower net price and patients moving to EYLEA HD [P10].
The largest positive contributor was the Sanofi antibody profit share, up 33.6% to $5,241.6m [D591][S52] and adding 9.3pp [D592], which the filing links to higher Dupixent sales [P9].
Operating expenses rose 5.4% [D457] against revenue growth of 1.0% [D440], so operating income fell 10.3% to $3,577.9m [D441][F20], a 4.4pp negative gap [D464].
Operating margin of 24.9% [F30] is the window low [D749], against a window median of 34.6% [D751] and a high of 55.7% in FY2021 [D750].
FY2018 and FY2019 table revenue is a later recast, $5,145.6m [F3] against $6,710.8m [X3] first reported and $6,557.6m [F4] against $7,863.4m [X4], so that median mixes two revenue bases.
In FY2025 R&D cut operating margin by 4.7pp [D465] as R&D rose 14.0% to $5,850.2m [D455][X34], while SG&A added 2.0pp [D466] after falling 8.6% [D456].
The filing attributes the SG&A fall to lower charitable contributions to the Good Days patient fund [P5][D456]; no cited passage explains the R&D increase [D455].

Net margin of 31.4% [F50] sits 6.5pp above operating margin of 24.9% [F30], as other income reached $1,652.8m [X117] from $789.2m [X116], a rise the cited filings do not explain; the effective tax rate was 13.9% [D427] against 7.7% [D378].
Operating cash flow of $4,978.9m [F80] was 1.11x net income [D428], and free cash flow of $4,080.5m [F100] was 0.91x net income [D429], below the peer median of 1.11x [D783].
Free cash flow margin of 28.4% [D425] is above the window median of 26.4% [D757]; capex rose 18.9% to $898.4m [D447][F90], 6.3% of revenue [D424] and 1.65x D&A [D430].
Conversion was weakest in FY2020, with free cash flow at 0.57x net income [D182], the window low [D761], as receivables rose partly from extended payment terms for EYLEA customers [P51].
Net cash was $16,879.9m [D434] at FY2025, from cash and investments of $18,865.8m [D432] less $1,985.9m of debt [F187], equal to 117.7% of revenue [D435].
Against eight biopharma peers [D780], net cash as a share of revenue ranks at the 100th percentile [D780] against a peer median of -50.7% [D781].
The current ratio of 4.13x [F180] is near its window median of 3.97x [D766], but return on average equity of 14.9% [D439] ranks at the 25th percentile [D784] against a peer median of 38.7% [D785].
In FY2025 buybacks of $3,438.6m [X137] and dividends of $370.3m [X140] took 93.3% of free cash flow [D437], after no dividends in FY2024 [X139], and diluted shares fell 5.6% in FY2025 [D459].
Returns now absorb nearly all free cash flow, so the net cash cushion depends on operating cash flow holding up.
Operating margin has fallen four years in a row, 30.7pp in total [R1], from 55.7% [F26] to 24.9% [F30].
The filings tie the FY2023 R&D rise to Sanofi no longer reimbursing half of Libtayo development costs [P24][D357], and the FY2024 SG&A rise to EYLEA HD launch spending [P14][D407].
Operating income fell 10.3% [D441] while net income rose 2.1% [D442], with other income at $1,652.8m [X117] against $789.2m in FY2024 [X116].
The cited filings do not explain the other income rise, and a release of tax liabilities helped hold the FY2025 tax rate of 13.9% [D427][P2], so FY2025 earnings lean on non-operating items.
Days sales outstanding were 146 at FY2025 [D438], against 160 in FY2024 [D389] and 101 in FY2016 [D19], with receivables of $5,741.1m [X197].
The filing ties the FY2020 receivables build to extended EYLEA payment terms [P51] and the FY2021 build to REGEN-COV sales [P39], but no cited passage explains the FY2025 level.
Operating margin: a reading below the FY2025 low of 24.9% [F30][D749] would confirm the decline, while a return above FY2024's 28.1% [F29] would reverse it; the FY2026 10-K will show this.
US EYLEA net sales: a further fall below $2,747.8m [S43] would confirm the sales pressure, while growth back above FY2024's $4,767.1m [S42] would reverse it; the FY2026 10-K will show this.
Shareholder returns: buybacks plus dividends above FY2025 free cash flow of $4,080.5m [F100][D436] would mean returns exceed cash generation; the FY2026 10-K will show this.
